html:
One of the largest and oldest covered markets in the world, in the old walled city of Istanbul. It grew up around a domed hall begun in 1455, two years after Mehmed II took Constantinople in the fall of the city.

Mehmed built the hall, the Cevahir Bedesten, as a strong, lockable store for valuable goods such as jewels, arms and fine cloth. Its rents went to a charitable trust that paid for the upkeep of Hagia Sophia, newly a mosque. A second hall followed, and over time the streets of shops between them were roofed over until they formed one huge market of many streets and thousands of shops.

Trades were grouped by street and run by guilds, which set prices and quality. The bazaar handled goods from across the Ottoman Empire and beyond, linking Istanbul with caravan cities such as Aleppo. Fires and an earthquake in 1894 damaged it many times, and it was rebuilt each time. It is still a working market and one of the city's most visited sights.
sum: One of the largest and oldest covered markets in the world, in the old walled city of Istanbul. It grew up around a domed hall begun in 1455, two years after Mehmed II took Constantinople in the fall of the city.
